name: Cushing Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guidelines for Cushing Syndrome

criteria.description: Elevated 24-hour urinary free cortisol (at least 2 measurements >3x upper limit of normal)
Failure to suppress cortisol on overnight 1 mg dexamethasone suppression test (cortisol >1.8 mcg/dL)
Elevated late-night salivary cortisol (at least 2 measurements above normal)
Loss of normal cortisol diurnal rhythm
ACTH level used to differentiate ACTH-dependent from ACTH-independent causes
High-dose dexamethasone suppression test or CRH stimulation test for ACTH-dependent differential
Characteristic clinical features (central obesity, striae, proximal myopathy, easy bruising)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: At least two abnormal first-line screening tests (24h UFC, late-night salivary cortisol, or 1 mg DST) confirming hypercortisolism, after exclusion of exogenous glucocorticoid use
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Cushing's disease specifically refers to pituitary ACTH-secreting adenoma (~70% of endogenous cases). Ectopic ACTH (~10-15%) and adrenal tumors (~15-20%) are other causes.

pathognomonic.notes: Highly specific for Cushing syndrome; typically on abdomen, thighs, breasts
searchTerms: large purple stretch marks over 1 cm

pathognomonic.symptomName: Proximal muscle weakness with preserved distal strength
pathognomonic.notes: Difficulty rising from chair or climbing stairs
searchTerms: weakness in upper arms and thighs
fat around trunk with thin limbs
thin arms and legs with belly fat

occasional.symptomName: Thin skin with poor wound healing

rare.notes: More common with ectopic ACTH secretion; very high cortisol levels overwhelm 11-beta-HSD2
searchTerms: low potassium and high blood pH

rare.notes: Due to very high ACTH stimulating melanocortin receptors; seen with ectopic ACTH

laboratory: Failure to suppress on 1 mg overnight dexamethasone suppression test
ACTH level: suppressed (<5 pg/mL) in adrenal causes; normal/elevated in ACTH-dependent causes
imaging: Pituitary MRI with gadolinium for Cushing's disease (may show microadenoma)
CT adrenals for ACTH-independent causes (adrenal adenoma or carcinoma)
CT chest/abdomen for ectopic ACTH source (bronchial carcinoid, SCLC, thymic carcinoid)
68Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT for occult ectopic ACTH source
genetic: MEN1 mutations in some pituitary adenoma cases
PRKAR1A mutations in Carney complex (primary pigmented nodular adrenocortical disease)
ARMC5 mutations in bilateral macronodular adrenal hyperplasia
USP8 mutations identified in some corticotroph adenomas
other: Bilateral inferior petrosal sinus sampling (BIPSS) to distinguish pituitary from ectopic ACTH

distinguishingFeatures: Metabolic syndrome lacks purple striae and proximal myopathy
Normal cortisol dynamics in metabolic syndrome
No muscle wasting in metabolic syndrome
PCOS has elevated androgens with normal cortisol
PCOS lacks purple striae and proximal weakness
Pseudo-Cushing responds to CRH-dexamethasone combination test
Lacks progressive physical stigmata of true Cushing

redFlags: Ectopic ACTH with severe hypokalemia and rapid onset (consider malignancy such as SCLC)
Very high cortisol levels with hyperpigmentation (suggests ectopic ACTH)
Adrenal mass >4 cm with rapid cortisol excess (concern for adrenocortical carcinoma)
Venous thromboembolism or opportunistic infections in untreated Cushing
Acute adrenal crisis after abrupt withdrawal of exogenous glucocorticoids or post-surgical hypocortisolism
references: Nieman LK, et al. The diagnosis of Cushing's syndrome: an Endocrine Society clinical practice guideline. J Clin Endocrinol Metab. 2008;93(5):1526-40.
Lacroix A, et al. Cushing's syndrome. Lancet. 2015;386(9996):913-27.
Newell-Price J, et al. Cushing's syndrome. Lancet. 2006;367(9522):1605-17.
Fleseriu M, et al. Consensus on diagnosis and management of Cushing's disease. Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol. 2021;9(12):847-875.
